section.heading: Determine Whether a Decimal is a Solution of an Equation
section.paragraph: Solving equations with decimals is important in our everyday lives because money is usually written with decimals. When applications involve money, such as shopping for yourself, making your family’s budget, or planning for the future of your business, you’ll be solving equations with decimals.

Now that we’ve worked with decimals, we are ready to find solutions to equations involving decimals. The steps we take to determine whether a number is a solution to an equation are the same whether the solution is a whole number, an integer, a fraction, or a decimal. We’ll list these steps here again for easy reference.

note.title: How To
note.heading: Determine whether a number is a solution to an equation.

list.item: Step 1. Substitute the number for the variable in the equation.
Step 2. Simplify the expressions on both sides of the equation.
Step 3. Determine whether the resulting equation is true. If so, the number is a solution. If not, the number is not a solution.

problem.paragraph: Determine whether each of the following is a solution of $$x - 0.7 = 1.5:$$

solution.paragraph: Since $$x = 1$$ does not result in a true equation, $$1$$ is not a solution to the equation.
Since $$x = -0.8$$ does not result in a true equation, $$-0.8$$ is not a solution to the equation.
Since $$x = 2.2$$ results in a true equation, $$2.2$$ is a solution to the equation.

section.heading: Solve Equations with Decimals
section.paragraph: In previous chapters, we solved equations using the Properties of Equality. We will use these same properties to solve equations with decimals.

row.cell: Subtraction Property of EqualityFor any numbers $$a,b, \text{and} c,$$ If $$a = b,$$ then $$a - c = b - c.$$
Addition Property of Equality For any numbers $$a,b, \text{and} c,$$ If $$a = b,$$ then $$a + c = b + c.$$
The Division Property of Equality For any numbers $$a,b, \text{and} c, \text{and} c \neq 0$$ If $$a = b,$$ then $$\frac{a}{c} = \frac{b}{c}$$
The Multiplication Property of Equality For any numbers $$a,b, \text{and} c,$$ If $$a = b,$$ then $$ac = bc$$

section.paragraph: When you add, subtract, multiply or divide the same quantity from both sides of an equation, you still have equality.

section.paragraph: Now that we have solved equations with decimals, we are ready to translate word sentences to equations and solve. Remember to look for words and phrases that indicate the operations to use.
